title: Curriculum Vitae
text:
Profile
Biostatistics leader pairing hands-on industry development and FDA regulatory experience across the drug-development lifecycle with a strong academic and methodological foundation. Currently Senior Manager, Biostatistics at Pfizer (Associate Director–equivalent) and a member of the Data Science & Analytics India leadership team, leading a team of statisticians across global Oncology and Inflammation & Immunology programs. Former FDA Oncology Center of Excellence primary reviewer with hands-on NDA/BLA experience, product-labelling negotiation, and pioneering use of real-world evidence and external-control cohorts.

Experience

Jun 2024 – present
Senior Manager, Biostatistics — Pfizer Healthcare India Pvt. Ltd., Chennai, India

Associate Director–equivalent statistical leader on the Data Science & Analytics India leadership team, shaping statistical strategy across global Inflammation & Immunology development programs.
Lead and develop a team of statisticians — building talent, strengthening statistical capability, and fostering a culture of scientific excellence.
Build enterprise capability in real-world evidence and target trial emulation, partnering with Statistics leadership to advance next-generation evidence generation.
Advance modern quantitative methods across programs, including endpoint consolidation, real-time trial monitoring, and reproducible quantitative science.



May 2022 – May 2024
Manager, Biostatistics — Pfizer Healthcare India Pvt. Ltd., Chennai, India

Trial-statistician leadership across Inflammation & Immunology programs spanning pediatric ulcerative colitis and inflammatory bowel disease, with medical-affairs support and priority programs in atopic dermatitis, asthma, and COPD — from study design through regulatory deliverables.
Oncology statistical leadership on targeted-therapy programs across non-small cell lung cancer and melanoma, spanning protocol design, analysis planning, and submission-supporting deliverables.

Reviewed applications spanning gastric and gastroesophageal cancers, cholangiocarcinoma, and additional solid-tumor indications, as well as an oncology biosimilar and a supportive-care (otoprotection) program.

Served as statistical consultant on cross-disciplinary research collaborations across the university.

Instructor, teaching assistant, and statistical consultant while completing PhD research.



Jun 2011 – Apr 2012

Supported early-stage sponsor studies through statistical programming, analysis, and study-support activities.

Research focus
Much of my recent work sits in two places: using target trial emulation to bring observational data to bear on questions trials answer slowly or not at all, and endpoint and estimand strategy — deciding what a trial should measure before arguing about how to analyse it.

title: A worked example: fuel economy in mtcars
text:
Weight against fuel economy
Heavier cars drink more, and the relationship is close to linear within each cylinder count.


Code
ggplot(cars, aes(wt * 1000, mpg, colour = cylinders)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.6, alpha = .85) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = FALSE, linewidth = .7) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("#2f6f4e", "#c08a2e", "#8c3b3b")) +
  labs(
    x = "Weight (lb)", y = "Miles per gallon", colour = NULL,
    title = "Fuel economy against weight",
    subtitle = "32 cars, Motor Trend 1974"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "top", plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))








Figure 1: Fuel economy falls with weight; the gap between 4- and 8-cylinder cars persists at any given weight.





Figure 1 is cross-referenced with @fig-weight-mpg — Quarto numbers the figure and makes the reference a link.

title: Setting up this site
text: This site is a Quarto website, edited in RStudio and hosted on GitHub Pages. The whole thing is plain text — .qmd files plus one YAML config — which means it versions cleanly in git and anything I can compute in R can go straight into a page.

title: Setting up this site
text:
Adding a post
Each post is a folder under posts/ containing an index.qmd:
posts/
  welcome/index.qmd
  my-new-post/
    index.qmd
    a-figure.png
The folder-per-post layout keeps images next to the text that uses them, and the published URL comes out as /posts/my-new-post/.
The front matter needs four things:
---
title: "The title"
description: "One line that shows up on the blog listing."
date: 2026-09-01
categories: [rstats, notes]
---
Then Render in RStudio, and the post appears on the Stuff page automatically — the listing reads the posts/ folder, so there’s no index to update by hand.

title: Setting up this site
text:
Why Quarto over R Markdown
Mostly that the website machinery is built in rather than bolted on, that freeze: auto means old posts don’t re-run their code on every build, and that the same .qmd can render to HTML, PDF, or slides without changing the source.

title: Abhishek Bhattacharjee, PhD
text:
I’m a biostatistician working at the intersection of clinical development, regulatory science, and real-world evidence.
I’m currently Senior Manager, Biostatistics at Pfizer in Chennai — an Associate Director–equivalent role on the Data Science & Analytics India leadership team — leading a team of statisticians across global Oncology and Inflammation & Immunology programs.
Before Pfizer I was a primary statistical reviewer at the FDA’s Oncology Center of Excellence, where I reviewed NDA, BLA, and IND submissions across several solid-tumor indications, led sponsor–agency labelling negotiations, and worked on one of the agency’s early evaluations of external-control cohorts in a pediatric neuroblastoma program. Earlier I was a tenure-track Assistant Professor of Statistics at the University of Northern Colorado.
What connects all of it: taking complex quantitative science and turning it into decisions people can actually act on.
